payload.description:
**Follow-on to PPY-156189** under `PPY-54055d`.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to flag brochure-speak and unsupported claims without treating Anth.us house voice as slop, so the steering queue on real articles is usable.

## Problem (dogfood on recent Anth.us posts)

Live diagnose on Sep 2026 posts over-flagged house style and under-used the avoid lexicon:

- `never` / `always` as English, not claims: always-on, always-available, never had a hook, never would have used them
- `missing_attribution` on list markers (`1.`, `2.`) and sticker numbers (`#247`)
- `uniform_cadence` on punchy short-sentence house voice (Thrifty Tokenmaxxing, Jevons)
- `redundancy` on intentional refrains ("Kanbus organized the work / It did not manage it")
- `voice_mismatch` swallowing whole openings because not every sentence has a contraction
- Style profile cannot enable/disable checks, so cadence cannot be turned down for this voice

## Done when

- Style profile can enable or disable each check (empty lead-in, list-shaped prose, vague claims, unsupported certainty, uniform cadence, redundancy, voice mismatch, missing attribution). Anth.us seed profile turns **uniform cadence off** (or equivalent: do not flag punchy short runs when sentenceStyle already prefers short/focused paragraphs).
- Unsupported certainty does not fire on `always-on`, `always-available`, `never had`, `never would`, or similar compounds / auxiliaries. It still fires on claim-level `everyone knows` / `undeniably` / bare `never` as universal claim.
- `missing_attribution` requires a statistical or quantitative *claim* (percent, multiplier like 10×, large counts with units), not list ordinals or `#247`.
- Redundancy does not treat a short heading/refrain repeated as a rhetorical beat (≤ ~12 words, or heading-only) as copy-paste slop.
- `voice_mismatch` findings are local (avoided term, or at most one sentence), not a multi-paragraph dump of contraction-free prose.
- Behave covers the false-positive cases above using fixtures drawn from the live dogfood, plus a still-positive brochure-slop fixture.
- `papyrus editorial diagnose` remains the operator/agent surface. Draft is still not rewritten.

## Out of scope

Rewrite options (PPY-73906c). Newsroom UI. Detector scores. Diagnosing raw MDX as a first-class format (operators use `article.md`).

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Diagnose respects house voice and optional checks
  As a publication operator
  I want diagnose findings I can actually steer
  So recent Anth.us articles are not a pile of cadence and never-word false positives

  Scenario: Always-on is not unsupported certainty
    Given a draft containing "Keep always-on rules thin" and "Grok Bot is always-available"
    And a loadable style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no unsupported_certainty finding whose excerpt is only those compounds

  Scenario: List ordinals are not missing attribution
    Given a draft whose only numbers are markdown list markers 1. and 2.
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no missing_attribution finding for those markers

  Scenario: Anth.us profile does not flag punchy cadence as slop
    Given the Anth.us style profile with uniform cadence disabled
    And a draft of five consecutive short punchy sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no uniform_cadence finding

  Scenario: Brochure slop still fires
    Given a draft that says "This will revolutionize workflows" and "Everyone knows agents will transform the industry"
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then findings include vague_claim or voice_mismatch for the avoided lexicon
    And findings include unsupported_certainty for "Everyone knows"

  Scenario: Rhetorical refrain is not redundancy
    Given a draft that repeats a short heading "It did not manage it" as a refrain
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then that refrain is not a redundancy group
```
payload.title: Tighten diagnose against house-voice false positives
